title: Validation, filters, and Problem Details in one screen
rememberThis: [ApiController] auto-validates data annotations to 400 ValidationProblemDetails — minimal APIs do not unless you add IEndpointFilter.
FluentValidation: separate validator classes, MustAsync for DB rules, TestValidate in unit tests, shared ValidationFilter<T> on MapGroup.
IAsyncActionFilter for controllers; IEndpointFilter for minimal APIs — middleware for transport-wide concerns only.
RFC 7807 Problem Details everywhere; put correlationId and error codes in extensions, not a parallel custom JSON envelope.
Outermost UseExceptionHandler + IExceptionHandler (.NET 8) + AddProblemDetails — exception filters alone are insufficient.
bullets: Model binding converts HTTP to types; validation checks rules — both can populate ModelState or filter errors.
IValidatableObject handles cross-property annotation rules; FluentValidation when rules grow or need async.
Setting context.Result in action filter or returning Results.* in endpoint filter short-circuits without running the handler.
CustomizeProblemDetails adds correlationId from X-Correlation-ID header or HttpContext.TraceIdentifier globally.
ValidationProblemDetails.errors maps property names to string[] — same shape for annotations, FluentValidation, and filters.
Integration-test a /throw route: assert 500 + application/problem+json + correlationId extension.
Problem Details vs custom errors: extensions.code for domain identity inside RFC 7807 — avoid { success: false } parallel schema.
